register: Idol self-post; mirror selfie in a bedroom
subject_scale: Mid-thigh up, about 85% of frame height
subject_placement: Centred; eyeline about 30% down from the top edge
camera_height: Chest height, level with the subject
pose_geometry: Square frontal, shoulders level, chin level, no twist. One arm raised to hold the phone at shoulder height, which is the only asymmetry in the figure
what_the_pose_is_for: Nothing. The pose is deliberately inert so the styling carries the frame
gaze_and_hands: Gaze straight into the lens through the mirror; free hand relaxed at the hip
makeup_placement: Rounded lash emphasis with no wing past the outer corner; brightened aegyo-sal under the eye; blush placed high and carried across the nose bridge; lip a blurred coral with no drawn lipline; brows light and low-arched, matched to the hair
makeup_contrast: Very low. Base, blush and lip sit within about two steps of each other, so the face reads as one tone with a flush
palette_structure: Warm-neutral room (beige wall, cream bedding) with a single saturated note in the sage dress. Two hues plus skin
light: Large soft source close and slightly above the face, frontal. Almost no shadow under the jaw
background_role: Set dressing that reads as a real bedroom; it locates the photo without competing
where_the_type_comes_from: None in the image. All type lives in the caption
impression_device: Costume-and-hair styling. Blunt bangs plus two low braids do the face-framing work a contour would otherwise do
transferable_rule: When the face is styled to a character, hold the pose still. A neutral frontal pose plus strong hair and wardrobe reads as intentional; the same wardrobe with an active pose reads as cosplay
what_this_cannot_tell_you: Whether the flush is product or grade. On a soft frontal key at this size the two are indistinguishable
do_not_copy: The face, the exact braid-and-bangs silhouette, and the dress. The transferable part is the light and the blush placement

frame_ratio: 4:5 canvas holding two smaller square insets
subject_scale: Each inset about 30% of canvas width, stacked with wide white margin
subject_placement: Insets centred on a plain white page, generous margin on all four sides
pose_geometry: Both arms raised above the head holding the product; elbows above the crown, torso in three-quarter, head tilted toward the raised arm
what_the_pose_is_for: Putting the bag above the eyeline. Held there, the product is the highest-contrast object in frame and the face becomes secondary
gaze_and_hands: Wide open-mouth smile with crinkled eyes; both hands occupied by the product
makeup_placement: Not readable at the delivered size; the visible decisions are a bright base and a warm lip
palette_structure: Butter yellow, white and black, with no third hue anywhere. Effectively two colours plus skin
light: Flat frontal, near shadowless, slightly blown in the highlights. The white-room-plus-window or on-camera-fill look
background_role: Plain wall, deliberately empty, so the striped knit is the only pattern
where_the_type_comes_from: None in the image; the brand and hashtags are in the caption
impression_device: Motion. Raised arms and a full smile signal a snapshot even though the post is paid
transferable_rule: To make a held product the subject, raise it above the eyeline. Height beats size: a small bag above the head outranks a large one at the hip
what_this_cannot_tell_you: Whether the collage or the pose drove the result. One post cannot separate them
do_not_copy: The outfit and the grin. What transfers is the product-above-eyeline rule and the two-hue discipline

subject_scale: Full figure at about 28% of frame height. Small on purpose
subject_placement: Centred, standing at the vanishing point of a receding colonnade
camera_height: Chest height, level, so the perspective lines stay straight
pose_geometry: Standing, both arms thrown up in a wide V, feet apart, weight even. An energy pose rather than a shape pose
what_the_pose_is_for: Nothing about the product. It converts a static corridor into a moment, and the corridor points at her
gaze_and_hands: Face too small to read; both hands open and raised
makeup_placement: Not assessable. At this scale the face carries no makeup information at all
palette_structure: Near monochrome: concrete grey, black trousers, white top, with one small green sliver of foliage at the left. One hue plus neutrals
light: Overcast ambient shade. No direct sun, no visible key, no shadow direction
background_role: The whole composition. Hard architectural lines converge on the subject; the background is the frame and the subject is the punctuation
impression_device: Scale inversion. Making the subject small in a strong one-point perspective reads as photography rather than advertising
transferable_rule: One-point perspective lets you shrink the subject without losing them, because the lines do the pointing. This is the cheapest way to make a phone photo look composed
what_this_cannot_tell_you: Nothing about the shoes, which are a few pixels tall. A product shot this wide is a brand post, not a product post
do_not_copy: The location. What transfers is the perspective device and the near-monochrome palette

register: Two paid posts on one account within four weeks
subject_scale: One tight collage versus one wide architectural frame
subject_placement: Product held to camera versus product almost invisible
what_the_pose_is_for: The comparison itself: which composition earned more on the same account, same format, same month
light: Blown frontal versus flat ambient shade
engagement_seen: 1.3M on the wide corridor versus 443.2K on the tight collage
transferable_rule: On a follower base this size the wide, photographic frame outperformed the tight product collage by roughly 3x. Where a brand demands product prominence, the cost is measurable and worth quoting back to them
what_this_cannot_tell_you: Nothing causal. Two posts, different products, different weeks, and no view counts. This is a prompt to test, not a finding
do_not_copy: Treating this as a rule. Run it as an A/B on the account that will actually carry the work

subject_scale: Three-quarter figure at about 75% of frame height
subject_placement: Left third. The right two-thirds is given entirely to the stadium
pose_geometry: Half back-turn: hips angled away, near shoulder rotated toward the lens, chin brought back over that shoulder. Weight on the far leg, contrapposto
what_the_pose_is_for: Showing the print on the back of the jersey while keeping the face to camera. The pose exists because the garment's graphic is behind
gaze_and_hands: Gaze to the lens over the shoulder; near hand raised to the hair, which lifts the arm clear of the jersey lettering
makeup_placement: Soft brown lash line, no wing, low-contrast base, glossy neutral lip. Nothing that competes with the daylight
makeup_contrast: Low, and low on purpose. High-contrast makeup in open shade at midday photographs as dirt
palette_structure: Green field, blue sky, white pinstripe. Three broad areas, no accent colour
light: Open daylight from camera right, backlit. The subject sits about a stop under the background with no fill, which is what makes it read as a real photo rather than a shoot
background_role: The reason for the post. Scoreboard, sponsor boards and turf are the caption
where_the_type_comes_from: Environmental signage already in frame, unreadable enough not to be an ad
impression_device: Access. The frame says she was let into a place the viewer cannot go, and the underexposure is what makes that read as documentation rather than a shoot
transferable_rule: When a garment's graphic is on the back, the pose is decided for you: rotate the hips away and bring the chin back. Then lift the near arm so it does not cross the print
what_this_cannot_tell_you: Whether the underexposure was chosen or accepted. Either way it is the look
do_not_copy: The person and the venue. What transfers is the back-print pose and the no-fill backlight

register: Promo post staged at a theme park
subject_scale: Full figure at about 90% of frame height
subject_placement: Right of centre, with two graphic signs stacked down the left third
pose_geometry: Standing, hips square, one hand behind the back, the other low. Still, because the frame is already busy
what_the_pose_is_for: Holding position inside a crowded frame. Any gesture here would collide with the signage
gaze_and_hands: Gaze to the lens, mouth closed and neutral; hands kept out of the silhouette
makeup_placement: Pink washed across the whole lid and carried under the lower lash line, giving a flushed halo around the eye; pale base; brow lightened to the hair
makeup_contrast: Deliberately unbalanced: the eye is the only saturated thing on the face, and the lip is left almost bare
palette_structure: Cold silver-blue hair against warm terracotta pavement, with magenta and yellow signage as the saturated accent. The coldest and warmest objects in frame are the subject and the ground
light: Overcast daylight, soft and directionless, which is why the saturated signage survives without clipping
background_role: A type carrier. The physical signs supply the headline
where_the_type_comes_from: The location. Nobody set type on this image; the park's own signs are the copy
impression_device: Environmental typography plus a pink eye that reads as recently crying
transferable_rule: Shoot beside the words instead of overlaying them. A real sign in frame beats a type layer, and it cannot be mistaken for a template
what_this_cannot_tell_you: Whether the signs were chosen or available. Either way the frame was built around them
do_not_copy: The character styling. What transfers is standing beside real type and the whole-lid pink placement

register: Backstage candid from a dressing room
frame_ratio: About 16:9, letterboxed inside the square canvas
subject_scale: Head and shoulders at about 80% of the strip height
subject_placement: Slightly left of centre; a flat ochre wall plane fills the right quarter
pose_geometry: Seated upright, shoulders square, head turned a few degrees off axis with the eyes following
what_the_pose_is_for: Nothing staged. The value is the absence of a pose
gaze_and_hands: Gaze just off the lens, lips slightly parted, no smile; hands out of frame
makeup_placement: Bare-look base with visible skin texture, brown lash line, glossy warm-rose lip, no hard blush edge, soft straight brows
makeup_contrast: Low overall but the lip is the one lifted element, which is what keeps a bare face from reading as tired
palette_structure: Warm amber and ochre throughout, oatmeal knit, brown hair. One temperature, no cool anywhere
light: Single warm source from camera left, tungsten-balanced, soft. Falloff visible on the far cheek
background_role: Left as found. A desk fan and dressing-room clutter are visible and were not cleaned up
impression_device: Curated candour. The environment is left messy while the face stays fully lit and finished
transferable_rule: Signal candour with the environment, not with the craft. Leave the clutter and the video-still crop, keep the light on the face deliberate. This out-earned every posed frame in the set
what_this_cannot_tell_you: Whether audiences reward the register or the person. A single account cannot separate the two
do_not_copy: The dressing room and the face. What transfers is the one-temperature grade and letting the background stay untidy
